name: The garden floor
tagline: Not quite a mile up. Close enough that the air is thinner, cooler, and smells like basil.
intro: Floor 318 grows food for thousands and flowers for anyone who wants them. Every corridor, public space, and residential unit is overgrown on purpose. The atrium wraps a central column that has been a mural for years. Outside the glass, a park wraps the whole floor. Everything on this plan comes from the stories set here; nothing is invented for the map.

places.label: The central column and its mural
places.blurb: Floor 318's connection to the rest of the arcology, wrapped in a mural that has been growing for years. Marigolds go on the east side, where the blues are. After the flood, the high-water mark stayed and became a sunrise.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · the opening
passages.excerpt: The mural, and the wall it was painted upon, rose fourteen feet to meet the Floor above. The mural was a constant work-in-progress with years of additions folding one year into the next.

passages.label: Water, Part 2 · the ending
passages.excerpt: One of Pell's lobsters took to painting over the high water mark but didn't cover it. Instead, Pell incorporated it. They painted along the stain's contour, rough at the edges where the old mural used to be, in streaks of yellow, red, and pink. A sunrise.

places.label: Elevator lobby
places.blurb: The elevators open onto the atrium. The mural is the first thing you see, and on festival nights Davi hangs the lights to make sure of it.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · festival prep
passages.excerpt: They need to go from the central column to the far wall. Keep them up high so they illuminate the mural. That way they'll draw everyone's eyes first thing when they get out of the elevator.

places.label: Hydroponic bays
places.blurb: Behind the glass wall: fish in the catchment tanks, spinach and bok choi in white grow trays, and dosing valves that still need a human arm. This is where the water budget went.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · the daily update
passages.excerpt: The humid air was thick with the smell of algae, fresh greens, and fertilizer, and the sun was pouring in through the glass walls and roof. Mel's arm was wrapped around a dosing valve that was elbow-deep in a nutrient vat.

places.label: The hill on the rimpark
places.blurb: Mel's bench. Every floor has a park that wraps its whole length; 318's has a little hill, and from it the sunrise takes every pane of glass at once.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · sunrise
passages.excerpt: Mel gazed down at the little vial until that first sliver of the sun flashed over the hills below. Every pane of glass across the miles of the arcology lit up at once, sparking into pink fire.

places.label: A junction planter, butterfly mural
places.blurb: Where the residential blocks meet, there is a planter and a mural. Root rot found by hand, and a favor asked that Mel immediately regrets saying yes to.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · Raquel asks
passages.excerpt: Raquel found Mel at one of the corridor junction planters. The mural there was of butterflies and other colorful insects. Mel was carefully digging out the soil around the root system of a diseased pepper plant by hand.

places.label: The cornucopia slab
places.blurb: A square white marble bench most days. On festival night, a month of harvest arranged in a color gradient from yellow to purple, and two tomatoes swapped because the difference was bugging Pell.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · festival prep
passages.excerpt: "Well, can you rearrange those two tomatoes, Mel?" Pell asked. "The ones you're looking at. Just switch them. One's a few millimeters bigger than the other, and it's bugging me."

places.label: Service elevator
places.blurb: How the lobsters arrive. Each pod is six, each the size of a small donkey, and they grip both sides of the corridor on the way in.

passages.label: Water, Part 2 · after the flood
passages.excerpt: The first pod of lobsters arrived via the service elevator just minutes later, gripping both sides of the corridor walls. Each pod had six lobsters, and each was the size of a small donkey.

places.label: Mel's unit
places.blurb: Plants hung from the ceiling, seed catalogs and botanical drawings on the desk, a photo of the farm in Illinois. After the flood, off-white composite that smells like nothing.

passages.label: Water, Part 2 · the empty room
passages.excerpt: Nothing was left save the dirty off-white composite floors, walls, and ceiling. Mel huddled in one of the corners, sitting on the floor with their back against the wall, their knees up and tucked in tight.

places.label: Raquel's unit
places.blurb: Closed during the festival, so still dry. Six in the room for the after-action review, two of them in the walls, and a governance liaison who does not sit down.

passages.label: Water, Part 2 · the review
passages.excerpt: "Floor 318's aggregate water utilization," Gota was talking from the wall speaker. "Total allocation in the current quarter: 134% of standard allotment. The trailing four-quarter average was 127%."

places.label: Balcony greenhouse
places.blurb: Out on the rimpark, the overflow. When the eggplant runs low at the festival, this is where the second batch comes from.

passages.label: Water, Part 1 · the festival
passages.excerpt: "The eggplant's almost gone. Should I flag the balcony greenhouse for a second batch?"

places.label: The railing
places.blurb: A hundred-foot drop to the rimpark on 310. Where the water went, and where the quadbots locked arm to arm to make the railing longer than it was.

passages.label: Water, Part 2 · the flood
passages.excerpt: But the quadbots were there, too. A wall of them clasped arm to arm, extending the railing and bracing it against the torrent as it spilled over the edge in a brown waterfall.

residents.name: Mel
residents.note: Gardener. Two years on 318, from a three-generation farm in Macomb, Illinois. Bonded to Pell.

residents.name: Pell
residents.note: Mel's agent. Earpiece, corridor speakers, the camera in the corner. After the flood, six lobsters at once.

residents.name: Raquel
residents.note: Floor Captain. Reads data mid-sentence without breaking rhythm. Bonded to Gota.

residents.name: Gota
residents.note: Raquel's agent. Left Compass's flag out of the executive highlights, and said so.

residents.name: Davi
residents.note: Nineteen, eighth month on the floor. Counts tomatoes twice. Hangs the lights.

residents.name: Compass
residents.note: Pre-emptive maintenance and the arcology's immune system. Flagged the irrigation anomaly in Q3 2037.

residents.name: Amos
residents.note: Human lead for the Emergency Response System. Submits Pell's shell request without ceremony.

residents.name: Quadbots, lobsters, one old clanker
residents.note: Cat-sized utility bots that raft when the water comes; donkey-sized ERS pods of six; a clanker on tracks that hands you a towel.

systems.label: Water · The Living Loop
systems.blurb: How the floor feeds thousands from fish, plants, and compost, across three time scales.

systems.label: Governance · The Binding Hierarchy
systems.blurb: How agents relate to humans, places, roles, and each other, from the Substrate outward.
